objective.objective: Recognise a square, a rectangle and a circle.

tasks.prompt: Watch straight side, corner, square corner and curved boundary demonstrated.
tasks.answer: A side here is a straight part of the boundary. A corner is where two straight sides meet. A square corner fits an undamaged square card corner exactly. objective.objective: Collect information about pupils' ages at home and school.

tasks.prompt: Watch permission, a consistent completed-years age question, two replies and accurate letter-labelled records.
tasks.answer: Mrs Binta asks permission and then asks each fictional role: How old are you in completed years? D replies 5 years and E replies 8 years; she records D=5, E=8 in labelled person-letter/age-in-years rows and checks each reply. Letters identify different fictional people, not age values or rank. A declined interview is replaced by a consenting adult role-playing a different fictional person. Reading this finished table is not interview performance.

tasks.prompt: Watch the completed two-column table and learn rows, columns and ordering ages.
tasks.answer: Completed model headings Person letter and Age in years, rows D/5 and E/8. Read across a row for one person, down the age column for ages. Five is less than eight, so the ages in least-first order are 5,8. Labels D and E identify people, not values or ranking. Later source practice uses a different fictional A6/B7/C6 dataset.

tasks.prompt: With support conduct two new fictional interviews and mark/compare/record two new full-size stand-ins; interpret the guided diagram separately.
tasks.answer: Supported age collection: ask permission and the identical completed-years question to two new adult fictional roles F and G, obtain replies only after asking, record labelled ages accurately and check back. Height: label two blank strips F/G, align bottom to each stand-in floor line, mark observed head tops, align bottoms, compare and record actual results. Fixed guided diagram F shorter than G, G taller than F is only interpretation, not evidence of new collection. Actual ages and heights are conditional; accept accurate different results and record support.

tasks.prompt: How old is practice pupil B?
tasks.answer: Practice B is 7 years old. This reads a supplied fictional record; it does not assess interviewing.

tasks.prompt: How many practice pupils are 6?
tasks.answer: Two practice pupils are 6: A and C.

tasks.prompt: Order the practice ages from least.
tasks.answer: Least-first ages are 6, 6, 7. Keep both 6s because two different people have that age.

tasks.prompt: Draw a pupil-letter/age table.
tasks.answer: Two labelled columns, Person letter and Age in years, with three rows A/6, B/7, C/6 when recording the supplied practice data. Any clear equivalent table is valid. Drawing/copying this table is separate from collecting new replies.

tasks.prompt: Why ask everyone the same age question?
tasks.answer: The same completed-years question makes replies about the same age meaning, allowing comparison. Obtain willing replies and record accurately; next-birthday age asks something different.

tasks.prompt: With consent, ask two willing people their ages in completed years and record letter labels and ages. One may be at home and one at school. If participation is declined, interview a teacher role-playing two people.
tasks.answer: Collect two new willing replies: ask permission, ask each the same completed-years question, listen, record unique person letters and ages with units, then check each reply back. Private consenting actual people or an adult playing two different fictional people are valid; fictional replies supplied only after each question. Accurate conditional replies, not a fixed printed answer. Decline is accepted; never publish identifiable real ages. Score asking and recording separately from reading or table drawing.

tasks.prompt: Before help explain then carry out new age interviewing/recording and new silhouette head-marking/comparison/recording.
tasks.answer: Recall permission and identical completed-years question; ask two new fictional roles, get replies after asking, record unique letters and accurate ages, check back. Recall safe same-baseline head-top marking for two new full-size paper stand-ins; make new labelled marks, align bottoms, compare and record both labels and actual taller/shorter/equal result. Record unaided recall first, then actual performance separately. No resources means actual collection not assessed; verbal recall is not practical evidence.

tasks.prompt: After recall, a smaller-step supported interview/record and new strip-mark/compare/record intervention.
tasks.answer: With support, model one permission request and identical completed-years question, then let child ask two fresh fictional roles and record checked letter/age replies.
